facts.function: Tough fibrous coat investing kidney; stretching causes flank pain (e.g. pyelonephritis)
facts.attachments: Surrounded by perirenal fat, then renal (Gerota) fascia, then pararenal fat

facts.function: Medial slit transmitting renal vein (anterior), renal artery, renal pelvis (posterior), nerves and lymphatics
facts.attachments: Opens into renal sinus; lies at about L1 (transpyloric plane)

facts.function: Cortex secretes aldosterone, cortisol, androgens; medulla secretes catecholamines
facts.innervation: Medulla receives preganglionic sympathetic fibers directly (thoracic splanchnic nerves)
facts.attachments: Cap superomedial poles of kidneys within renal fascia; right pyramidal, left crescent-shaped
facts.supply: Superior (inferior phrenic), middle (aorta), inferior (renal) suprarenal arteries; right vein → IVC, left → left renal vein

facts.function: Outer kidney layer containing glomeruli and proximal/distal convoluted tubules; extends between pyramids as renal columns
Inner region made of renal pyramids; loops of Henle and collecting ducts concentrate urine via countercurrent mechanism
facts.supply: Vasa recta; relatively hypoxic, vulnerable to ischemic injury

facts.function: Cone-shaped medullary units (~8–18); base faces cortex, apex forms renal papilla; contain loops of Henle and collecting ducts
Cortical tissue extending between renal pyramids; carries interlobar arteries and veins
Apex of each pyramid; papillary ducts empty urine into a minor calyx; papillary necrosis with NSAIDs, sickle cell, diabetes
Cups around each renal papilla collecting urine; several unite to form a major calyx
Usually 2–3 per kidney; formed by minor calyces, drain into renal pelvis; staghorn calculi fill them
Funnel-shaped upper ureter in renal sinus collecting urine from major calyces; ureteropelvic junction is common obstruction site
Carry urine by peristalsis to bladder; stones lodge at ureteropelvic junction, pelvic brim, ureterovesical junction
facts.innervation: Renal/hypogastric plexuses; pain referred loin to groin (T11–L2)
facts.attachments: Renal pelvis → on psoas → crosses iliac bifurcation at pelvic brim → under uterine artery/ductus deferens → bladder
facts.supply: Segmental branches of renal, gonadal, aorta, common/internal iliac and vesical arteries

facts.function: Supplies abdominal viscera and walls: celiac, SMA, renal, gonadal, IMA and lumbar branches
facts.attachments: Aortic hiatus (T12) → descends left of IVC → bifurcates at L4 into common iliac arteries

facts.function: Returns blood from below diaphragm to RA; receives renal, right gonadal, right suprarenal and hepatic veins
facts.attachments: Union of common iliac veins at L5 → ascends right of aorta → caval opening (T8) → right atrium

facts.function: Paravertebral ganglion chain giving splanchnic nerves to renal and hypogastric plexuses (vasoconstriction, bladder filling/storage)
facts.innervation: Preganglionics T1–L2; kidney via lesser/least thoracic and lumbar splanchnics (~T10–L1)
facts.attachments: Lumbar part runs on anterolateral vertebral bodies along medial border of psoas

facts.function: Supply kidneys (~20–25% of cardiac output); stenosis causes renovascular hypertension
facts.attachments: Abdominal aorta at L1–L2 below SMA → right longer, passes behind IVC → anterior/posterior divisions → segmental arteries

facts.function: Drain kidneys into IVC
facts.attachments: Left longer, crosses anterior to aorta beneath SMA (nutcracker), receives left gonadal and suprarenal veins; right short

facts.function: Foregut artery: stomach, liver, gallbladder, spleen, part of pancreas, proximal duodenum
facts.attachments: Anterior aorta at T12 → left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries

facts.function: Midgut artery: distal duodenum to proximal two-thirds of transverse colon
facts.attachments: Anterior aorta at L1 below celiac → passes over left renal vein and third part of duodenum

facts.function: Hindgut artery: distal third of transverse colon to upper rectum
facts.attachments: Anterior aorta at L3 → left colic, sigmoid and superior rectal arteries

facts.function: Supply testes (testicular) or ovaries (ovarian)
facts.attachments: Anterior aorta at L2 below renal arteries → descend on psoas, crossing ureter anteriorly → deep inguinal ring or suspensory ligament

facts.function: Drain testes (from pampiniform plexus) or ovaries
facts.attachments: Right → IVC directly; left → left renal vein at right angle, so left varicocele is more common

facts.function: End arteries supplying renal vascular segments; no anastomoses, so occlusion causes segmental infarction
facts.attachments: From anterior and posterior divisions of renal artery in renal sinus → interlobar arteries

facts.function: Supplies superior (apical) segment of kidney
facts.attachments: Usually from anterior division of renal artery

subs.name: Anterior division (anterosuperior and anteroinferior segmental arteries)

facts.function: Supplies anterior kidney via anterosuperior and anteroinferior segmental arteries
facts.attachments: Anterior branch of renal artery, passing anterior to renal pelvis

facts.function: Supplies inferior pole segment of kidney
facts.attachments: Usually from anterior division of renal artery

facts.function: Supplies posterior segment of kidney
facts.attachments: Posterior division of renal artery, passing posterior to renal pelvis

facts.function: Laterally flexes trunk and fixes 12th rib in inspiration; posterior relation of kidney
facts.innervation: Subcostal nerve (T12) and ventral rami L1–L4
facts.attachments: Iliac crest and iliolumbar ligament → 12th rib and L1–L4 transverse processes

facts.function: Flexes hip (with iliacus as iliopsoas); posterior relation of kidney and ureter; psoas sign with retroperitoneal inflammation
facts.attachments: T12–L5 vertebral bodies, discs, transverse processes → lesser trochanter of femur

facts.function: Anterosuperior tip of bladder facing pubic symphysis; continues as median umbilical ligament (urachus remnant)
Main part of bladder between apex and fundus; rises into abdomen when full (palpable suprapubically)
Posterior surface of bladder facing rectum (male) or vagina (female); contains trigone internally
Inferior, most fixed part of bladder leading into urethra; rests on prostate in males
Smooth muscle of bladder wall; contracts to empty bladder during micturition
facts.innervation: Pelvic splanchnics (S2–S4, parasympathetic, M3) contract; sympathetic (β3) relaxes during filling

facts.function: Smooth triangle between two ureteric orifices and internal urethral orifice; derived from mesonephric ducts
Opening of bladder into urethra at inferior apex of trigone; prostatic enlargement can obstruct it
Involuntary smooth muscle at bladder neck; maintains continence and prevents retrograde ejaculation in males
facts.innervation: Sympathetic (T10–L2 via hypogastric nerve, α1) contracts; parasympathetic relaxes

facts.function: Voluntary skeletal muscle around membranous urethra; provides voluntary continence
Slit-like ureter openings at posterolateral angles of trigone; oblique intramural course acts as flap valve against vesicoureteral reflux
Conveys urine (and semen in males) from bladder to exterior
facts.attachments: Female ~4 cm, opens anterior to vagina (UTI-prone); male ~20 cm: prostatic, membranous, spongy parts

facts.function: Widest, most dilatable part; receives ejaculatory ducts at seminal colliculus and prostatic ducts; compressed in BPH
Shortest, narrowest, least distensible part, surrounded by external urethral sphincter; injured in pelvic fractures
Longest part, within corpus spongiosum; receives bulbourethral gland ducts; bulbar part injured in straddle injuries
Male: slit at tip of glans (narrowest point; ventral in hypospadias); female: in vestibule between clitoris and vaginal opening
Supply pelvis and lower limbs
facts.attachments: Aortic bifurcation (L4) → divide at sacroiliac joint/pelvic brim into internal and external iliacs; ureter crosses here

facts.function: Drain pelvis and lower limbs
facts.attachments: Internal + external iliac veins → unite at L5 to form IVC; left compressed by right common iliac artery (May–Thurner)

facts.function: Supply pelvic viscera, perineum, gluteal region and medial thigh
facts.attachments: Common iliac at sacroiliac joint → anterior division (vesical, uterine, internal pudendal, obturator) and posterior division

facts.function: Drain pelvic viscera (via pelvic venous plexuses), perineum and gluteal region
facts.attachments: Tributaries accompany internal iliac branches → join external iliac vein at pelvic brim → common iliac vein

facts.function: Main supply to lower limb; gives inferior epigastric and deep circumflex iliac arteries
facts.attachments: Common iliac → along pelvic brim on psoas → femoral artery beneath inguinal ligament

facts.function: Drain lower limb and lower anterior abdominal wall
facts.attachments: Continuation of femoral vein at inguinal ligament → joins internal iliac vein to form common iliac vein

facts.function: Supply superior bladder and distal ureter
facts.attachments: Branches of patent proximal umbilical artery (anterior division of internal iliac)

facts.function: Motor to external urethral and anal sphincters and perineal muscles; sensory to perineum and external genitalia
facts.attachments: Exits greater sciatic foramen → around ischial spine/sacrospinous ligament → lesser sciatic foramen → pudendal canal

facts.function: Secondary cartilaginous joint uniting pubic bones; bladder lies directly behind it (retropubic space)
facts.attachments: Fibrocartilaginous disc between pubic bodies; reinforced by superior and inferior pubic ligaments

facts.function: Forms most of pelvic floor; supports pelvic viscera, resists intra-abdominal pressure, aids urinary and fecal continence
facts.innervation: Nerve to levator ani (S4) and pudendal nerve (inferior rectal) branches
facts.attachments: Pubic bodies, tendinous arch of obturator fascia, ischial spines → perineal body, anococcygeal ligament, coccyx

facts.function: Main part of levator ani; supports pelvic viscera around urethra, vagina and rectum
facts.innervation: Nerve to levator ani (S4) and pudendal nerve (inferior rectal) branches
facts.attachments: Posterior pubic body and anterior tendinous arch → anococcygeal ligament and coccyx

facts.function: Thin posterolateral part of levator ani supporting pelvic floor
facts.innervation: Nerve to levator ani (S4) and pudendal nerve (inferior rectal) branches
facts.attachments: Posterior tendinous arch and ischial spine → coccyx and anococcygeal ligament

facts.function: U-shaped sling around anorectal junction maintaining anorectal angle; key to fecal continence, relaxes for defecation
facts.innervation: Nerve to levator ani (S4) and pudendal nerve (inferior rectal) branches
facts.attachments: Pubic bodies → loops behind anorectal junction (no bony insertion)

facts.function: Secretes PSA-rich seminal fluid into prostatic urethra; BPH arises in transition zone, carcinoma in peripheral zone (DRE)
facts.attachments: Base at bladder neck → apex on urogenital diaphragm; posterior surface palpable through rectum
facts.supply: Inferior vesical (prostatic) arteries; prostatic venous plexus drains to internal iliac and vertebral plexus (bone metastases)

facts.function: Site of implantation and fetal development; usually anteverted and anteflexed over bladder
facts.attachments: Between bladder (vesicouterine pouch) and rectum (rectouterine pouch); held by cardinal and uterosacral ligaments
facts.supply: Uterine artery (internal iliac), crossing superior to ureter ('water under the bridge')

facts.function: Stores feces before defecation; lies posterior to bladder/prostate (male) or uterus/vagina (female)
facts.attachments: Continues sigmoid colon at S3 → anorectal junction at puborectalis sling
facts.supply: Superior (IMA), middle (internal iliac) and inferior (internal pudendal) rectal arteries

facts.function: Fibromuscular canal: menstrual outflow, copulation and birth canal; lies posterior to bladder and urethra, anterior to rectum
facts.attachments: Cervix → opens into vestibule
facts.supply: Vaginal and uterine arteries (internal iliac); upper lymph to iliac, lower to superficial inguinal nodes

facts.function: Terminal GI outlet; continence via internal (involuntary smooth) and external (voluntary skeletal) anal sphincters
facts.innervation: Above pectinate line visceral (painless); below via inferior rectal nerve (pudendal), painful
facts.supply: Above pectinate: superior rectal artery; below: inferior rectal artery
